questions.title: Assembly language program
questions.text:
**Assembly language mnemonics**

| Mnemonic | Description |
|---|---|
| INP | Retrieve user input and store it in the Accumulator. |
| OUT | Output the value stored in the Accumulator. |
| LDA | Load the Accumulator with the contents of the memory address given. |
| STA | Store the value in the Accumulator in the memory address given. |
| ADD | Add the contents of the memory address to the Accumulator. |
| SUB | Subtract the contents of the memory address from the Accumulator. |
| BRP | Branch/Jump to the address given if the Accumulator is zero or positive. |
| BRZ | Jump to the address given in case the Accumulator is zero. |
| BRA | Jump to the address given. |
| HLT | Stop the code. |
| DAT | Used to associate a label to a free memory address. An optional value can also be used to be stored at the memory address. |

Assembly language instructions are written as mnemonics.


questions.title: School football team
questions.text:
A school has a football team. The team consists of 1 goalkeeper and 10 players whose positions depend on the tactical formation chosen.

Tactical Formations (10 players):

- 4-4-2: 4 defenders, 4 midfielders, 2 forwards.
- 4-3-3: 4 defenders, 3 midfielders, 3 forwards.
- 3-5-2: 3 defenders, 5 midfielders, 2 forwards

parts.title: School football team (a)(i)
parts.text:
The team coach needs a program that checks if the team is formed according to one of the three tactical formations.

If the formation is correct, the algorithm should output a confirmation message. Otherwise, it should display a message indicating that the formation does not exist.

To perform the check, the coach needs to enter values into the following variables:

- def – for defenders
- mid – for midfielders
- fwd – for forwards

Write pseudocode or code in a programming language for this algorithm.

scheme.mark_scheme:
INPUT def
INPUT mid
INPUT fwd (1)
IF (def == 4 AND mid == 4 AND fwd == 2) THEN
    PRINT "The team division matches the 4-4-2 formation."
ELSE IF (def == 4 AND mid == 3 AND fwd == 3) THEN
    PRINT "The team division matches the 4-3-3 formation."
ELSE IF (def == 3 AND mid == 5 AND fwd == 2) THEN
    PRINT "The team division matches the 3-5-2 formation."
ELSE
    PRINT "The team division does not match any standard tactical formation."
END IF
[5]
1 mark for inputs; 1 mark for correctly implementing the if statements; 1 mark for correctly using logical conditions; 1 mark for the output of confirmation message; 1 mark for the output when condition is false. Accept any valid alternative solutions.
scheme.model_answer:
INPUT def
INPUT mid
INPUT fwd
IF def = 4 AND mid = 4 AND fwd = 2 THEN
    OUTPUT "The team division matches the 4-4-2 formation."
ELSE IF def = 4 AND mid = 3 AND fwd = 3 THEN
    OUTPUT "The team division matches the 4-3-3 formation."
ELSE IF def = 3 AND mid = 5 AND fwd = 2 THEN
    OUTPUT "The team division matches the 3-5-2 formation."
ELSE
    OUTPUT "The team division does not match any standard tactical formation."
ENDIF

questions.title: Substitutions
questions.text:
In a football game, 11 players are on the field, and 3 substitute players are waiting to play. It is allowed to make three substitutions. When a substitution is needed, the coach selects the player on the field and the substitute player, swaps them and updates his data.

Array fieldP represents the players on the field. Array subP represents the substitute players.

For example, at the beginning of a game:

`fieldP = [11, 2, 8, 4, 5, 10, 7, 3, 9, 6, 1]`

`subP = [12, 13, 14]`

At the end of that game:

`fieldP = [11, 2, 8, 4, 13, 10, 14, 12, 9, 6, 1]`

`subP = [3, 5, 7]`

parts.title: Substitutions (a)
parts.text: Determine the indexes of the first and last elements for the array fieldP.

scheme.model_answer: First index 0, last index 10
scheme.ai_instructions: Also accept 1 and 11 if the candidate clearly states arrays indexed from 1.

parts.title: Substitutions (b)
parts.text: Write pseudocode or code in a programming language for the coach that will update the arrays when a substitution is made.

scheme.mark_scheme:
fieldP[11] ← [11, 2, 8, 4, 5, 10, 7, 3, 9, 6, 1]
subP[3] ← [12, 13, 14]
INPUT s1, s2
FOR i FROM 0 TO 2
    IF subP[i] = s2 THEN
        FOR j FROM 0 TO 10
            IF fieldP[j] = s1 THEN
                subP[i] ← fieldP[j]
                fieldP[j] ← s2
            ENDIF
        ENDFOR
    ENDIF
ENDFOR

1 mark for initialising arrays; 1 mark for declaring variables and getting input for making a substitution; 1 mark for correct use of loop (subP); 1 mark for condition finding the substitute player from subP; 1 mark for correct use of loop (fieldP); 1 mark for condition finding the substituted player from fieldP; 1 mark for correct substitution.
[Max: 7] Accept any correct solution (C++, Python and pseudocode versions are given in the mark scheme).
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept any correct solution in pseudocode or a programming language.

parts.title: Substitutions (c)
parts.text: Write pseudocode or code in a programming language to sort the array fieldP in ascending order using insertion sort.

scheme.mark_scheme:
for i in range(1, len(fieldP)):
    key = fieldP[i]
    j = i - 1
    while j >= 0 and key < fieldP[j]:
        fieldP[j + 1] = fieldP[j]
        j -= 1
    fieldP[j + 1] = key

1 mark for the correct external loop with the correct range; 1 mark for defining the key; 1 mark for defining the variable j; 1 mark for the correct internal loop; 1 mark for correctly swapping the elements.
[Max: 5] Accept valid alternative algorithms.
scheme.model_answer:
for i in range(1, len(fieldP)):
    key = fieldP[i]
    j = i - 1
    while j >= 0 and key < fieldP[j]:
        fieldP[j + 1] = fieldP[j]
        j -= 1
    fieldP[j + 1] = key
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept valid alternative insertion-sort algorithms (e.g. swapping adjacent elements). Do not accept bubble sort.

questions.title: Predicting match results
questions.text:
Calculations can be used to predict football match results. The probability of how many goals each team will score in the match is calculated using the Poisson distribution:

P(k; λ) = (λ^k · e^(−λ)) / k!  — that is, λ to the power k, multiplied by e to the power −λ, divided by k factorial.

Where:

- λ — the average expected number of goals (intensity).
- k — the number of goals.
- P(k; λ) — the probability that the team will score k goals.

The pseudocode for Poisson distribution is presented:

```pseudocode
VAR Ep REAL
VAR Poisson REAL
INPUT L
INPUT K
Lp = 1
FOR i from 1 to K DO
   Lp = Lp * L
ENDFOR
e = 2,71828
term = 1
FOR i from 1 to L DO
   term = term * e
ENDFOR
Ep = 1 / term
factorial = 1
FOR i from 1 to K DO
   factorial = factorial * i
ENDFOR
Poisson = (Lp * Ep) / factorial
OUTPUT K
```

[Max: 2] 1 mark for the method of optimisation; 1 mark for explaining how efficiency is improved. Accept valid alternative answers.
scheme.model_answer: Replace the loop Lp = Lp * L with Lp = L^K; this replaces K repeated multiplications with one operation.

This removes unnecessary intermediate variables (1)
[2] 1 mark for the method of optimisation; 1 mark for explaining how efficiency is improved. Accept valid alternative answers.
scheme.model_answer: Calculate L^K directly inside the Poisson formula instead of storing it in Lp; this removes an unnecessary intermediate variable, so less memory is used.
